title: Answer whether multi-floor buildings should be one file per floor (matching UVTT) or one consolidated file, distinguishing the import boundary from this project's own authoritative storage
objective: Owner asked, following the UVTT 2D-to-3D reconciliation just recorded, whether this project's own multi-floor building storage should mirror UVTT's one-file-per-floor convention or consolidate all floors into a single file. Answering by distinguishing three distinct layers that this question actually spans, rather than picking one global answer: (1) the import boundary, which is necessarily one-file-per-floor because that is how external tools (Dungeondraft, DungeonFog, Foundry's Levels module) already produce UVTT data -- not a choice this project gets to make; (2) this project's own authoritative runtime state, which per DEC-016/section 15 of GRAFTING_MASTER_SOURCE.md is already a single unified Snapshot with a journal, not per-entity files -- floors are just entities/regions with a Z-offset attribute inside that one state, so 'one file per floor' would actually be a step backward from the already-decided single-Snapshot architecture; (3) an authoring/export/sharing file format (if the project ever wants GMs to export/share a building as a portable file), where a single consolidated 'building bundle' file (each floor as an internal array item, reusing UVTT-shaped per-floor fields for simplicity) is recommended over N separate files, since it guarantees floor-to-floor referential integrity (Z-offsets, stairwell connections, building-wide metadata) by construction rather than needing a separate manifest to keep N files in sync.
validations: Extended the 'Import (Tier 2): Universal VTT (UVTT)' section's reconciliation paragraph in docs/research/vtt-map-and-terrain-construction-options.md with a concrete answer to the file-structure question, distinguishing the import boundary (necessarily one-file-per-floor, dictated by external tools) from this project's own authoritative state (already a single Snapshot per DEC-016, not per-entity files -- recommending against introducing per-floor files there) from an optional future authoring/export bundle format (recommending one consolidated file per building, each floor as an internal item, for referential-integrity reasons).

Grounded the 'authoritative state is not file-based' claim directly in the already-established DEC-016/section 15 architecture (journal + periodic snapshots) rather than asserting it fresh, keeping this consistent with the rest of the document.
No dependency installed, no code written, no ADR reopened -- documentation reasoning only, building on already-established architecture, no new external research needed for this specific question.
artifacts: docs/research/vtt-map-and-terrain-construction-options.md (Import (Tier 2) section extended with the file-structure recommendation)
risks: This is a design recommendation, not a decision -- the owner may choose differently once actual authoring/export UX is designed.
No dependency installed, no code written -- research/documentation only.
